title: Nexus Between Financial Technology and Financial Inclusion in Sub-Saharan Africa: A Dynamic Panel Technique
decision_rationale: Own two-step system GMM estimation on 29-30 SSA economies. Exposure is a PCA index of mobile subscriptions and internet subscriptions (plus population density and size), which meets the mobile/internet exposure criterion; outcome is financial inclusion (family 5). Borderline on exposure because the label is 'fintech' and two of four index inputs are demographic.
exposure_measure: Financial technology index (FT): PCA composite of mobile subscriptions per 100 (MOB), internet subscriptions per 100 (INT), population density (POD) and population size (POS); min-max normalised. The first component loads mainly on MOB and INT, the second on POS (Table 8, Eq. 14). The exposure variable is therefore mobile/internet penetration blended with demographic variables, not a direct measure of fintech products.

sample.economies_or_groups: selected Sub-Saharan African countries (list not given in the text read)
sample.income_groups_covered: not reported (SSA only; no income-group split)

design.estimator: two-step system GMM (dynamic panel); Hansen and Sargan tests, AR(1)/AR(2)
design.key_controls_fixed_effects: lnRGDP, trade openness, inflation, human capital (primary enrolment), deposit interest rate, lnremittances, government consumption, real interest rate, institutional quality

results.indicator: Financial inclusion index (FI), PCA of ATMs and commercial bank branches (levels, per adults, per km2)

results.evidence: Table 10 col (3), p.11; text p.10 'availability does not have a significant impact'

confounding_reverse_causation.why: Causal language ('effect', 'determinant'), but the only strategy is internal system-GMM instruments with 12-14 instruments for 29 groups; reverse causality is acknowledged (authors claim bi-directional causality) but no causality test is shown. Sargan p=.008 in the usage model, AR(2) p=.065 in the FI model.

exposure_measurement.why: FT index mixes mobile and internet penetration with population density and size, and the second retained component is dominated by population size; it does not purely capture technology adoption and is not fintech/mobile money use.

selection_of_countries_years.why: 30 SSA countries chosen by data availability; missing values filled with regional means and 3-year moving averages, which can induce artificial smoothness.

outcome_measurement.why: FI index built only from supply-side ATM and commercial-bank branch counts (and per capita/per km2 versions); omits account ownership, mobile money and digital finance, which is the channel of interest. Usage and availability sub-indices are built from overlapping variables.

specification_and_researcher_degrees_of_.why: Two-step PCA weights, imputation, and instrument-set choices are discretionary; text refers to ARDL and unit-root tests that are not used in the final estimator; inconsistent counts of countries and observations.

selective_reporting.why: Only one specification per outcome and no robustness checks; conclusion text contradicts Table 10 on several points (see notes).

venue_quality_concern: possible (open-access SAGE Open; large internal inconsistencies between text and tables)
notes: Eligibility judgement: fintech as labelled is not itself an eligible exposure, but the operational variable is a mobile/internet penetration index (MOB and INT dominate component 1), so included as mobile/internet exposure; reviewer may reasonably flag as borderline. Outcome is financial inclusion only (family 5); no output or productivity outcome (real GDP is a control). Inconsistencies: 30 countries stated but 29 groups and 512 obs in Table 10 vs 540 obs in Table 3; conclusion says HC significant at 1% and negative, but Table 10 shows HC insignificant for FI; Conclusion says FT significant for availability whereas Table 10 shows 0.3381 insignificant; FT said to be I(1) in some unit-root tests yet GMM described as conforming to ARDL; Findex 2021 is cited as a source but the index uses FAS supply data. Minus signs appear as '2' in the converted text (e.g. '20.0980' = -0.0980), so FT coefficients printed without a leading 2 are read as positive; the minus-sign reading of the control coefficients is a conversion artefact. No text aimed at the extractor was found.
